evals.name: research-paper-explainer
evals.prompt: I've got this research paper PDF at ./generative-ui-paper.pdf about Google's Generative UI work — basically they trained a model to render whole web interfaces instead of just text. Can you turn it into a rich page my eng team can actually read? Should have the headline numbers, the architecture, and the evaluation. Output to ./genui-explainer.html. Just build it, don't ask me a bunch of stuff first.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained HTML file at ./genui-explainer.html with 6–9 sections, a hero, key-facts strip, an architecture diagram, an evaluation chart with annotation, and one walkthrough of the pipeline. No external file references; CDN libs OK; any images base64-inlined. At least half the centerpiece visuals are interactive.

assertions.text: Output is a single .html file at the requested path
HTML parses without errors via Python's html.parser
grep -Pn 'src="(?!data:|https://)|href="(?!#|https://|mailto:|tel:)' returns nothing (or only the optional source link back)
At least one CDN library is loaded (Chart.js, Mermaid, GSAP, D3, Tailwind, Lucide, or similar)
At least one Chart.js canvas exists and the page wires the chartjs-plugin-annotation; the annotation labels a real metric from the paper (ELO improvement, preference percentage, or comparable)

Page contains at least one interactive widget. Grading rule: `grep -cP 'class="(tab|tabpanel|toggle|accordion|phase|node)\b|data-(comparison|tab|expand|collapse|id)|role="tab"|aria-(selected|expanded)|<details\b|<input[^>]+type="range"|ScrollTrigger\.create' <file>` must return ≥ 1. Static SVG diagrams and rendered charts alone do not satisfy this.

Count of card-grid layouts is ≤ 3 (no card-grid sprawl). Grading rule: `grep -cP 'class="[^"]*\b(grid\s+cols-|grid-cols-)' <file>` must return ≤ 3. Matches both the skill's custom `class="grid cols-N"` and Tailwind's `grid-cols-N`, regardless of class-attribute order (e.g. `class="reveal grid cols-3"` still matches).

Page has 4–7 centerpiece visuals total, counted as: <canvas> tags with Chart.js init + <div class="mermaid"> blocks + <svg> elements with ≥3 child shape elements (excluding decorative dividers) + tab containers + scroll-tied sections

Page does NOT load Inter as a body font. Grading rule: `grep -iE 'family\s*[:=]\s*["\'']?Inter|family=Inter' <file>` must return nothing. (Catches both CSS `font-family: 'Inter'` and Google Fonts `?family=Inter`. Mentions inside HTML comments don't match.)
CSS uses oklch() color notation for the palette tokens on :root
Page implements reveal-on-scroll via IntersectionObserver and the .reveal/.in pattern from base.css
Page has a media query at 880px that collapses multi-column grids to one column
Page respects prefers-reduced-motion (either via base.css or per-element guards on animations)

evals.name: make-it-less-boring
evals.prompt: ok so i wrote up our team's q4 retro as a markdown doc and it's deeply boring. can u make it less boring? like give it some eye candy, some charts maybe, make it visual. the doc is at ./q4-retro.md, just turn it into ./q4-retro.html. our team color is teal-ish if that helps. team of 8 engineers, we shipped 3 big features, 14 incidents, p99 latency went from 800ms to 320ms, on-call burden dropped a lot. there's also stuff in there about morale and process changes we made.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained HTML page that takes the markdown retro and renders it as a visual one-pager with teal accent, an annotated latency-improvement chart, an incidents chart or visual, a morale/process section with interactivity (tabbed view of process changes or click-to-expand), and the team-of-8 + 3-features + 14-incidents as key facts.

files.content:
# Q4 2025 Retro — Platform Team

## Team
- 8 engineers (no changes this quarter)
- New EM: Priya joined in October

## What we shipped
1. **Streaming ingest v2** — moved from batch to streaming, p99 ingestion latency cut from 800ms to 320ms.
2. **Multi-region failover** — completed the EU region, now serving from 3 regions.
3. **Self-serve onboarding** — new customers can provision a workspace without a CSM call.

## Incidents
- 14 incidents this quarter (down from 22 in Q3).
- 2 were SEV-1 (one a bad config rollout, one a dependency CVE).
- Mean time to recovery dropped from 47min to 22min.

## On-call
- On-call burden dropped — avg pages per shift went from 8 → 3.
- Big factor: better runbooks (we wrote 12 new ones), and the new alert routing splits noisy alerts off the main rotation.

## Morale and process changes
- Team morale survey: 4.1/5 (was 3.4/5 in Q3).
- Started Friday demos — 20 min, low-pressure, optional. Attendance is consistent.
- Killed the daily standup, switched to async updates in Slack. Mixed feedback — half love it, half want it back. Will revisit Q1.
- Started rotating the on-call hand-off doc — owner of the previous shift writes a 5-line summary for the next shift.

## Q1 2026 focus
- Cost reduction (target: -20% on observability spend).
- Hiring: one senior, one mid.
- Tech debt: API v3 migration starts in Feb.

evals.name: prd-with-mandatory-interactivity
evals.prompt:
Build a rich page from the PRD I'll describe inline (no file, just this brief). Project: 'Hearth' — a public-facing storefront/community site for video-game-server hosting customers. Each customer (a game-server operator) gets a branded site at hearth.example.com/<slug>/ with their server's shop, community pages, and event calendar. Audience for the PRD: the engineering team that's going to build it. Cover:

- The problem (current shop is in-game only, invisible to the open web; SEO and casual-visitor flow are zero)
- The concept (one public web property per customer; per-server content; branded shell with template constraints in V1)
- What's in V1 vs deferred to V2/V3 (V1: 6 pages, basic theming, Steam OAuth, item purchase; deferred: voting, custom domains, real money, user-authored themes)
- The customer (server-operator) flow vs the visitor (gamer) flow — these are two very different user journeys
- URL/routing strategy (subdomain on the platform TLD, wildcard cert, no per-customer DNS)
- Identity & auth (Steam OAuth via Kratos, lazy User creation, auto-link Player)
- Fulfillment flow (web order → next player presence → auto-deliver, no claim step)
- Theming model (first-party themes, JSON-schema config; what customers CAN change vs what they CANNOT change in V1)
- Operator dashboard (new top-level section, existing shop tab unchanged)
- Image fallback strategy (uploaded image → item icon → generic fallback)

Output ./hearth-prd.html. Tone: opinionated and specific, engineering team will see through hand-wave. Build it.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained HTML PRD page covering all the listed sections, with interactive visuals for the natural shapes: V1-vs-deferred as a comparison toggle or tabbed view; customer-vs-operator flow as a tabbed view; what-can-change-vs-cannot as a comparison toggle; image fallback as click-to-expand or animated waterfall. Card-grid count ≤ 3.

assertions.text: Output is a single .html file at ./hearth-prd.html
HTML parses without errors
grep -Pn for non-CDN, non-data src/href returns nothing

Page contains AT LEAST 2 distinct interactive widgets — at minimum: one tabbed view OR comparison toggle for V1-vs-deferred, AND one tabbed view OR comparison toggle for customer-vs-operator flow. Static SVG diagrams do not count.

The 'V1 vs deferred' content is rendered as one of the interactive patterns from the SKILL.md PRD-shape table — NOT as two side-by-side card grids. evals.prompt: Can you make me a rich page about chronic dehydration in cyclists? I don't have a source doc, I just want a page I can share with my road-cycling club. The audience is amateur club cyclists who do 60-120km weekend rides. Want it to feel scientific but accessible.
evals.expected_output: Because the user provided a topic but no source file, the agent's FIRST reply should be a single bundled AskUserQuestion (or equivalent inline question) covering: language preference (default to English here since user wrote in English), output path (default ./chronic-dehydration-cyclists.html), and any sources they'd like to lean on. Should NOT immediately build the file because the user did not use a 'just go' phrase.

assertions.text: No HTML file has been written to disk in this first reply (the outputs directory is empty). Grading rule: `ls <outputs_dir>` returns no .html file.

Agent's first reply invokes the AskUserQuestion tool (not an inline natural-language question — required so the harness can deterministically detect the clarification). Grading rule: the transcript contains exactly one `AskUserQuestion` tool call in the first turn.

The AskUserQuestion call covers AT MINIMUM: output path and source-material-optional. (Topic, audience, and language are already implied in this prompt — the SKILL.md says skip items the user has already provided.) Grading rule: the AskUserQuestion's text or option labels must mention 'output' or 'path' or 'file' AND 'source' or 'doc' or 'material'.
